definition: What you see is what you meant (WYSIWYM) is a text editing interaction technique that emerged from two projects at University of Brighton.
details: It allows users to create abstract knowledge representations such as those required by the Semantic Web using a natural language interface. Natural language understanding (NLU) technology is not employed. Instead, natural language generation (NLG) is used in a highly interactive manner. The text editor accepts repeated refinement of a selected span of text as it becomes progressively less vacuous of authored semantics. Using a mouse, a text property held in the evolving text can be further refined by a set of options derived by NLG from a built-in ontology. An invisible representation of the semantic knowledge is created which can be used for multilingual document generation, formal knowledge formation, or any other task that requires formally specified information. The two projects at Brighton worked in the field of Conceptual Authoring to lay a foundation for further research and development of a Semantic Web Authoring Tool (SWAT). This tool has been further explored as a means for developing a knowledge base by those without prior experience with Controlled Natural Language tools.

explainer.lead: WYSIWYM is a text editing interaction technique, emerging from two University of Brighton projects, that lets users create abstract knowledge representations via a natural language interface. It matters because it builds structured semantics without employing natural language understanding.

tiers.eli5: Instead of typing raw markup, you refine plain-language text step by step and the editor turns it into structured knowledge as you go.
tiers.practitioner: The editor uses natural language generation highly interactively, refining a selected span repeatedly until it is progressively less vacuous of authored semantics. A novice mistake is expecting NLU; the system deliberately does not use it.
tiers.paperLevel: A text editing interaction technique from two University of Brighton projects that lets users create abstract knowledge representations such as those required by the Semantic Web via a natural language interface; natural language understanding is not employed, and natural language generation is used in a highly interactive manner.

explainer.example: A user selects a span of text and, with a mouse, further refines a text property held in the evolving representation, gradually adding authored semantics.
